key_insight: Zatom-2 is a unified atomistic generative foundation model that jointly pretrains on large molecular and material datasets to improve generation, structure prediction, and force/energy prediction across domains.
engineering_relevance: This approach can accelerate materials and molecular design workflows by providing a transferable model for both organic and inorganic atomistic tasks, including low-data protein generation.
method: Pretrained on ~5 million structures from OMol25 and OMat24.
Uses a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching.
Supports generation, structure prediction, and force-conditioned energy/force prediction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved molecular distribution fidelity over Zatom-1, strong benchmark performance for molecule and material generation, and protein backbone designability rising from 67.8% to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown across several benchmarks, but transfer to new domains may still depend on dataset quality, force-conditioning setup, and the availability of task-specific finetuning data.
paper_title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
